operations: Sishen mine: open-pit iron ore mine near Kathu, ~14 km long, one of the largest open pits in the world; jig plant (world's largest) and DMS plant; R11.2bn Ultra-High Dense Media Separation (UHDMS) project under construction (~45% complete, main tie-in Aug/H2 2026) to lift premium product to 55% and extend LOM to 2041. Operated by Sishen Iron Ore Company (Pty) Ltd (SIOC): Kumba Iron Ore 76.3% (Anglo American ~70% of Kumba), Exxaro Resources 20.37%, SIOC Community Development Trust 3.06%, SIOC Employee Share Ownership Trust. No ownership change; Anglo-Teck merger keeps Kumba in portfolio.
scale_note: 2025 production 25.3 Mt (Kumba total 36.1 Mt); 2026 guidance ~22 Mt (UHDMS tie-in); waste 135-145 Mt/yr; on-mine unit cost R530-560/t. Renewables: embedded solar offtake agreement with Envusa Energy (Anglo American / EDF power solutions JV) signed July 2026 - 72.5 MWp DC / 63 MW AC PV on the G80 waste rock dump inside the mine boundary, first power Q4 2027, completion 2028, ~35% of Sishen scope 2 emissions; lifts Kumba renewable penetration to ~45%. Fatality-free >10 years.

operations: Kolomela mine: open-pit iron ore mine ~22 km from Postmasburg (Ga-Segonyana/Tsantsabane), in production since Dec 2011; seven open pits incl. Leeuwfontein, Welgevonden, Kapstevel, Klipbankfontein; conventional drill/blast, shovel-and-truck; produces high-strength lump ore; Ploegfontein concept study complete, pre-feasibility started 2026. Same owner/operator as Sishen: SIOC (Kumba 76.3%, Exxaro 20.37%, community and employee trusts). Mine office: 20 Main Street, Postmasburg.
scale_note: 2025 production 10.8 Mt; 2026 guidance ~10 Mt with waste stripping 45-50 Mt (higher strip ratio); on-mine unit cost R430-460/t; LOM 14 yrs (Kumba targeting 20+). Renewables: 11 MW wheeled renewable electricity from Envusa Energy's Koruson 2 cluster (MooiPlaats Solar 240 MW, Umsobomvu Wind 140 MW, Hartebeesthoek Wind 140 MW) since March 2026 - ~72-84% cut in Kolomela scope 2 emissions; ~72% of Kolomela electricity now renewable. Fatality-free >3 years.

operations: Black Rock Mine Operations (BRMO): three underground mechanised bord-and-pillar manganese complexes - Nchwaning 2 (shaft 421 m, commissioned 1981), Nchwaning 3 (shaft 500 m, 2004/05) producing high-grade oxide ore, and Gloria (140 m, 1975) producing medium-grade semi-carbonate ore - ~75-80 km NW of Kuruman near Hotazel; surface beneficiation plants, stockyard, rail loop and rapid load-out; R10.2bn Black Rock and Gloria expansion completed 2022 (target 4.6 Mtpa); underground battery-electric loaders and trucks, remote operations centre. Owner Assmang (Pty) Ltd, 50% African Rainbow Minerals (ARM Ferrous) / 50% Assore; ARM provides administration and technical functions, Assore sales and marketing. No ownership change. Coordinates are the Nchwaning shafts.
scale_note: ~4.2-4.3 Mt manganese ore per year (ARM: 4.3 Mt; IMnI: 4.2 Mt), majority exported via Port Elizabeth/Saldanha; employees 2,541 permanent + 3,273 contractors (assmang.co.za) / 4,233 total (ARM); LOM >30 years; 12 million fatality-free shifts May 2024. No renewable PPA or on-site solar found in official sources (none in ARM 2025 ops review or Assmang site).

operations: N'Chwaning (Nchwaning 1/2/3) shafts are the core of Assmang's Black Rock Mine Operations together with Gloria - one operation, one mining complex, one management (BRMO senior general manager). Not a separate mine. See o_mu8ko0n7_41wug.
scale_note: Included in Black Rock Mine figures (~4.2-4.3 Mtpa, ~5,800 people).

operations: Hotazel Manganese Mines (HMM): Mamatwan open-cut mine (terrace mining, DMS and sinter plant; coordinates given) and Wessels underground mine (vertical and incline shafts, mechanised bord-and-pillar, ~300 m; -27.2000, 22.9667) in the Kalahari Manganese Field; site office 1 Peperboom Avenue, Hotazel 8490, tel +27 53 742 2300. HMM (Pty) Ltd is held via Samancor Manganese: South32 44.4% (operator), Anglo American 29.6%, B-BBEE entities 26%. Wessels was shut Dec 2024 and reopened Jan 2025 on weak prices; Metalloys smelter sold June 2025. Same operation as the existing 'South32 South Africa Manganese' record.
scale_note: FY25 saleable production 2,151 kwmt (100% basis); FY26 2,085 kwmt; FY27 guidance 2,000 kwmt (subject to continued higher-cost trucking); Mamatwan ~2.9 Mtpa ROM, ~15 yrs life; 10-year Transnet MECA3 rail/port export contract signed Aug 2025. No renewable PPA disclosed for HMM (South32 SA renewable work referenced only at Hillside).

operations: Black Mountain Mine (BMM) at Aggeneys = the Deeps underground mine (vertical shaft, ~1 Mtpa, Cu-Pb-Zn-Ag) and Swartberg underground mine (decline, ~0.9 Mtpa, Cu-Pb-Ag), a 1.65 Mtpa concentrator and assay lab; Deeps approaching end of life, Swartberg expansion (open pit 1.5 Mtpa, 13 extra years) under way with a strategic mining partnership with Inayo Mining signed 12 Feb 2026. Held by Black Mountain Mining (Pty) Ltd: Vedanta 69.6%, Exxaro Resources 24.4%, ESOP 6%; operated by Vedanta Zinc International (head office Sandton, +27 11 685 3960). Mine lies immediately west of Aggeneys town (town 29.200S 18.850E) - no mine-specific coordinates in an official source. This is the 'Black Mountain Mining' record already on file.
scale_note: FY24 ~75 kt metal-in-concentrate from Deeps + Swartberg; >1,200 people directly and indirectly. Renewables: Phase 1 of VZI Renewable Energy Programme - PPA with Enernet Global (Aug 2023) for a 12 MW DC solar PV plant for BMM, ~29 GWh/yr, 25-year term, construction from Q1 2024; Phase 2 = wheeled off-site renewables for Gamsberg; target 76% renewable energy by 2027, carbon neutral 2040.

operations: Gamsberg zinc mine: open pit on the Gamsberg inselberg ~20 km east of Aggeneys with dedicated concentrator and robotic assay lab; Phase 1 designed for 4 Mtpa ore / 250 ktpa zinc-in-concentrate (running ~400 kt ore/month); Phase 2 (R5.5bn, approved March 2022, groundbreaking Aug 2022) doubles to 8.5 Mtpa ore / 500 ktpa metal-in-concentrate with a second concentrator now in construction; opened Feb 2019; LOM 30-50 years. Part of Black Mountain Mining (Pty) Ltd (Vedanta 69.6%, Exxaro 24.4%, ESOP 6%) - the existing 'Black Mountain Mining' record covers it; General Manager: Gamsberg is David Malunga (on file).
scale_note: >1,200 permanent employees (>2,000 incl. indirect); Phase 2 adds 600-1,000 permanent jobs; reserves/resources >180 Mt at 6-6.5% Zn (Phase 2 lifted VZI ore reserves to 525 Mt). Renewables: VZI Phase 2 plan is wheeling off-site renewable energy across the Eskom grid to offset Gamsberg, Phase 3 for Gamsberg Phase II - no signed Gamsberg PPA found; group target 76% renewable by 2027.

operations: Cullinan Diamond Mine (formerly Premier), ~40 km east of Pretoria: underground block cave and sub-level cave (C-Cut), with approved C-Cut Extension and CC1-East projects; mining possible into the late 2040s. Owned by Cullinan Diamond Mine (Pty) Ltd: Petra Diamonds 74%, Kago Diamonds 14%, Itumeleng Petra Employee Trust 12%; Petra operator since 2008. Petra SA office +27 11 702 6900, procurement mailbox GRP_Vendors@petradiamonds.com.
scale_note: FY2025: 1.45 million carats, 4.7 Mt treated; ~2,200 employees and contractors. Renewables: long-term PPAs with Etana Energy (licensed trader) signed May 2024 for wheeled wind/solar supplying 36-72% of Cullinan's and Finsch's load from FY2026, supporting a 35-40% Scope 1+2 cut vs 2019.

operations: Finsch Diamond Mine at Lime Acres, ~160 km NW of Kimberley: underground sub-level cave (Block 5); Finsch Diamond Mine (Pty) Ltd owned Petra 74%, Kago Diamonds 14%, Itumeleng Petra Employee Trust 12%. STATUS CHANGE: Petra placed Finsch into business rescue on 29 May 2026 (BRPs Daniel van Jaarsveld and Luke Saffy took custodianship 10 June 2026); production suspended June 2026; on 7 Aug 2026 creditors approved an asset-sale plan after the BRPs found no viable way to restart - the mine is being wound down/sold, ending ~60 years of operation. Cyril Dakada (on file as COO) is described on Petra's leadership page as General Manager of Finsch.
scale_note: FY2025 (last full year): 975,828 carats, 2.2 Mt treated, ~1,700 employees and contractors, ~34% of Petra revenue; >90% of stones under 2 ct. Etana Energy wheeled-renewable PPA (May 2024) also covered Finsch - now moot.

operations: Koffiefontein underground diamond mine (kimberlite pipe). Petra placed it on care and maintenance in November 2022 and, after DMPR section 11 consent, completed the sale of Blue Diamond Mines (Pty) Ltd (the holding company) to Koffiefontein Holdings (Pty) Ltd, an affiliate of the Dubai-based Stargems Group, by end October 2024 for nominal cash; Stargems assumed rehabilitation and care-and-maintenance liabilities. Stargems also owns Jagersfontein and Rooipoort. No public statement found on a restart, current management or employee numbers since the sale; Wikipedia still (wrongly) shows Petra as owner.
scale_note: Historic production 7.3 million carats; 2021 resource ~5.25 Mct; last active output before 2022 was small. No renewable PPA known.
status_flag: sold - now Stargems Group (Koffiefontein Holdings (Pty) Ltd)

operations: No mine of this name could be found. The DMPR Northern Cape operating-mines table lists 'Lambasi Iron Ore Mine | Anglo American | Iron Ore | Open-pit | Operating | Namakwa', but Anglo American/Kumba's only iron ore mines are Sishen and Kolomela (Gamagara/Ga-Segonyana districts) and Anglo has no iron ore asset in Namakwa. The only 'Lambasi' on Anglo/Kumba web properties is the Lambasi agricultural initiative supported by the Anglo American Zimele fund (an Eastern Cape farming project), which appears as a link on every angloamericankumba.com page - the DMPR row looks like a scraping/data error. No people, no coordinates, no website.
status_flag: doubtful - no Anglo American iron ore mine called Lambasi exists; DMPR row appears erroneous; 'Lambasi' is a Zimele-funded agricultural initiative referenced on Kumba's site

operations: Thabazimbi Iron Ore Mine: historic open-pit iron ore mine (since 1931) in the town of Thabazimbi. Closure decided 2015 and mining ceased 1 September 2016 under Kumba/SIOC; transferred to ArcelorMittal South Africa for R1 plus liabilities (agreement Feb 2017, section 11 cession 2018) - now Thabazimbi Iron Ore Mine (Pty) Ltd, 100% AMSA, reported under AMSA 'Non-Steel Operations'. Since then the site is in rehabilitation (R85m spent 2025, down from R115m as AMSA tries to 'unlock additional ore') with re-handling/beneficiation of historic ROM stockpiles and discard dumps for Vanderbijlpark; no open-pit mining. AMSA CEO Kobus Verster and CFO Gavin Griffiths are on file.
scale_note: Supplied 227,940 t beneficiated iron ore to Vanderbijlpark in 2025, planned 240,000 t in 2026; ~63 employees transferred at the 2017 handover. No renewable PPA.

operations: Foskor Mining Division, Phalaborwa: open-pit phosphate mine on the Phalaborwa Igneous Complex (North Pyroxenite pit since 1966, South Pyroxenite pit; historic Foskorite pit ~2 km wide), with crushing, milling (Loesche and ball mills) and flotation to produce phosphate rock concentrate railed to Foskor's Richards Bay acid division; magnetite stockpiles. Foskor (Pty) Ltd shareholders: IDC 59%, Manyoro Consortium 15%, Coromandel International 14%, Kopano Foskor Employees Trust 6%, Ba-Phalaborwa and Umhlathuze Community Trusts 5%, Sun International FZE Dubai 1%. Leadership change: Foskor's site now lists Ms NP Zulu as Interim CEO (Ufikile Khumalo on file no longer shown); COO MJ (James) Morotoba. HQ tel +27 11 347 0600 (Midrand).
scale_note: ~2.2 Mt phosphate rock concentrate per year (Foskor RFP 2025/26); FY2024 (Mar) 1,577 kt phosphate rock (FY2023 1,933 kt); group 1,716 permanent employees / 2,233 incl. contractors across Phalaborwa, Richards Bay and Midrand. No renewable PPA or on-site solar found for Foskor Phalaborwa (neighbouring Palabora Mining Company signed a 132 MWp + 360 MWh Marula Green Power PPA in 2025).
